title: Plumbline fact bundle v1 — manifest
description: A bundle is a zstd-compressed tar. This schema describes manifest.json, its index member; the layout it indexes is specified in docs/DATA-MODEL.md section 6. Read support for every historical bundle schema is permanent: a bundle is an archival artifact, and if an old bundle cannot be re-evaluated the core promise of the product is broken. Write support is current-version only.

bundle_id.description: Random 128-bit identifier assigned at collection. Not derived from host identity, so it leaks nothing under --redact.

catalog_version.description: Catalog present at collection time. Informational only: a bundle may be evaluated against any later catalog, which is the entire point of bundles.

redacted.description: True when --redact was used. Redaction happens at collection time, so a redacted bundle is safe to attach to a bug report.

meta_member.description: Host descriptors: os-release, kernel, arch, hostname. Partially populated or absent when redacted.

capabilities.description: Privileges actually held during collection. Explains why a collector was skipped.

network_used.description: False for every v1 scan. Set only by explicitly opted-in collectors such as CLOUD in v2, so a reader can tell whether the offline invariant held for this bundle.

facts.description: Index of facts/<id>.json members. A reader that does not recognise a fact ID preserves it opaquely rather than failing to open the bundle.

fact_version.description: A check that does not understand this version resolves to UNKNOWN(fact_version_mismatch). It never attempts a best-effort read: a best-effort read of a misunderstood structure is exactly how a false PASS is produced.

evidence.description: Content-addressed raw sources under evidence/<sha256>.blob, deduplicated across all citing checks.

truncated_sources.description: Sources that exceeded the read cap. Findings citing these are annotated rather than silently treated as complete.

errors_member.description: Every fact error, retained so a gap can be explained months later.

signed.description: Whether a detached signature accompanies this bundle. Integrity is NOT authenticity: integrity.json proves the archive is internally consistent, not that it came from anyone in particular. Only a detached signature proves origin, and renderers must state the difference. Conflating the two was audit finding A-14.
